findings.summary: Memory create_run and create_run_idempotent accept a RunRecord whose conversation_id names no conversation; Postgres refuses with a raw psycopg ForeignKeyViolation outside the port vocabulary; no both-stores test.

Memory update_run and wait_for_approval accept a changed conversation_id (re-linking bypasses the one-active-run check); Postgres refuses with a raw CheckViolation; the only test is Postgres-only and asserts the driver exception.
One active run per conversation holds only while create_run_in_conversation is the sole creator of linked runs; nothing enforces the premise.
No test pins that a same-key retry with a different request digest returns the recorded digest, which 4d.1's CONFLICT decision needs.
The memory concurrency tests never interleave (an uncontended asyncio.Lock does not yield), so they cannot fail without _conversation_lock.
The created_at expression orders in the database default collation while the id tie-break uses COLLATE C; correct today with fixed-width UTC strings.
A duplicate run_id in _admit raises a raw UniqueViolation on Postgres while memory raises ConcurrencyConflict.
Close ritual pending; FB-2, migration 0007 safety, paging, NotFound and lock order otherwise check out.
